fediverse.page.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
fediverse.page.check.inbox-refusals: Deliveries refused in the last 24 hours
fediverse.page.fix.url-missing: Set URL to the CMS's real public origin, for example https://cms.example.com, and restart. Activities sent in the background build their ids from it.
fediverse.page.fix.url-not-https: URL should be the public https origin. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, set URL to the https address and make sure the proxy forwards X-Forwarded-Proto.
fediverse.page.fix.actor-key-unreadable: The stored actor key cannot be read. Restore the database from a backup taken before the problem: a new key would be a new identity for every follower.
fediverse.page.fix.actor-key-missing-enc: ENCRYPTION_KEY is not the value the actor key was encrypted with. Put the previous value back and restart; the stored key is left untouched.
fediverse.page.fix.webfinger-skipped: The WebFinger check needs URL: set it first.
fediverse.page.fix.webfinger-unreachable: The CMS could not reach its own public address. Check DNS, the proxy and the firewall, and that URL is the address remote servers use.
fediverse.page.fix.webfinger-not-found: The public address answered, but not with the WebFinger document. Make sure /.well-known/* and /fediverse/* reach the CMS and are not intercepted by the frontend or a proxy rule.
fediverse.page.fix.webfinger-wrong-subje: The public address answered with a different account. Check the username in the site settings (Fediverse profile) and that the domain in URL is the CMS's.

fediverse.panel.problem.not-failed: There is no failed delivery to retry for this article.
fediverse.page.fix.actor-key-missing: No actor key is stored yet. It is created the first time a remote server fetches the actor or an activity is sent; fetch the actor's address once, or publish an article. If followers already exist, the key was lost: restore the database from a backup.
